contradictions.topic: The header-field toggle that suppresses the company address is written "Company Name Without Address" in title case as a section heading and "Company Name without address" in lowercase in running prose and in the guide revision history.

The guide-level revision history, which is the only place the field and the Purchase Order Configuration window are named together, writes it in lowercase as "Company Name without address".

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Match this control case-insensitively. Probe the title-case form "Company Name Without Address" first (it is the section heading, so most likely the rendered group label), and fall back to the lowercase "Company Name without address" form, which is how both the running prose and the only by-name page attestation write it. Never fail the step on a case mismatch alone.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis: SAP's section headings are auto-title-cased by the help-portal toolchain while the prose and revision history preserve the original UI string, which would make the LOWERCASE form the more likely on-screen label. Stated as a hypothesis - the corpus never shows the rendered control.

contradictions.topic: The header-field toggle that omits the requestor's name from the ship-to address is written "Ship To Without Requestor Name" in the section heading and "Ship To without Requestor Name" in the body sentence of the same topic.

This is intra-file heading-versus-prose drift, not a documented UI variant, and it is emitted because a case-sensitive driver would fail on it - not because two sources disagree about the product.

contradictions.topic: Who owns the From-address prefix for PO transmission emails, and at what point in the lifecycle - the Invoice Configuration administrator on the Purchase Order Configuration tool, or the PO Processor at transmit time in the Preview Purchase Order window.

readings.summary: The admin-guides roster places the prefix on the Default Sender Email field of the configuration tool and assigns the change to admins, with a documented default of PurchaseOrder.
readings.sourceQuote: type in a desired prefix in the Default Sender Email field

readings.summary: The tools-guides preview topic gives the same prefix lever to the PO processor inside the Preview Purchase Order window, at transmit time, well after the configuration is set.
readings.sourceQuote: The processor can change the prefix for the From address but cannot change the suffix of the address from "\_DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com".

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: Set the prefix in Purchase Order Configuration, but do NOT treat the configured value as authoritative on the wire: verify the actually-sent From address on a transmitted PO rather than asserting it from configuration alone, and do not build any check that assumes the configured prefix is what the vendor sees. Both topics agree the suffix "_DoNotReply@ConcurSolutions.com" is immutable, so only the prefix is in dispute.
contradictions.notes: Hypothesis, stated as a hypothesis: these are probably COMPLEMENTARY surfaces rather than a genuine product conflict - the admin sets a default and the processor overrides it per transmission. The corpus never says so. It never states whether the processor's change is per-transmission or persists, never states whether the processor's change writes back to the configuration, and never states which wins if both are set. Recorded because the ambiguity is material to anyone configuring the sender address, not because SAP asserts two incompatible facts.
